title: Structured Output Quick Cards + Inline Validator Launch Screens
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a compact, low-friction onboarding surface for structured output (JSON schema) that explains schema basics with example quick-cards and demonstrates an inline validator state machine. This ticket covers art direction for the launch screens, copy variants, and final product screenshots for release notes and docs.
acceptance_criteria: Three quick-card variants (basic, typed example, edge case) with copy and example prompts ready for implementation
Inline validator UI states designed: empty, valid, warnings (type coercion), and errors (schema mismatch)
High-fidelity screenshots captured at 1440px showing validator overlays and token-cost meter for docs and release notes
Accessibility pass: contrast checks documented and all interactive labels provided
Handoff package delivered in Figma with redlines, tokens, and developer annotations
tasks: Audit existing schema onboarding assets and list gaps (done 2026-02-26)
Design three compact quick-card layouts optimized for mobile and desktop
Create inline validator microcopy for error/warning/guide states
Design token-cost meter visual to appear alongside examples
Prepare final product screenshots with realistic prompt and model output
Handoff to engineering with Figma redlines, CSS token spec, and accessibility notes
decisions: Use compact quick-cards instead of full walkthrough to reduce friction for power users
Show validator warnings (type coercion/suggestion) instead of blocking errors by default; provide toggle for strict mode
Include token-cost meter on examples to educate users about cost/length tradeoffs
Use neutral brand palette for validator states (amber for warnings, red for errors, teal for valid) to avoid strong emotional cues
comments: 2026-02-26 - Maya Chen: Initial audit complete; found inconsistent validator microcopy across console and docs
2026-03-01 - PM feedback (Eleanor Park): Prefer showing warnings inline rather than blocking on first-run to avoid user drop-off
2026-03-03 - Engineering (Diego Ramos): Confirmed feasibility for inline validation hooks; requested final state list and sample payloads
2026-03-05 - Design review (Aria Patel): Adjust contrast on warning chips; increased padding on quick-card CTA

notes_for_engineering: Validator states should be driven by a validation API that returns {status, messages, suggestions} — map status to UI states: empty|valid|warning|error
Quick-cards are content-only components with optional 'Use example' buttons that prefill the prompt input
Token-cost meter should reflect token estimate from server; use provided token-estimate endpoint for examples
Provide CSS tokens for chip colors: --rv-chip-warn, --rv-chip-error, --rv-chip-valid
test_plan: Smoke: verify quick-cards render and 'Use example' prefills prompt
Validation states: feed known good, coercible, and invalid payloads to validator and capture UI
Accessibility: keyboard-only flow for quick-cards and validator overlay, run axe-core scans
Screenshots: capture at 1280x and 1440x using the latest console build for release assets
